extracted.intended_audience: prospective participants in USPTO pro bono programs (independent inventors, small businesses, volunteer patent practitioners, law school clinics, and clearinghouse organizations)
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO slide guidance describing the goals, eligibility criteria, volunteer qualifications, matching procedures, and scope for Patent, PTAB, and TTAB pro bono programs, plus Law School Clinic and LEAP participation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Pro Bono Program purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent inventors and small businesses who are financially under-resourced are matched with volunteer practitioners to prepare, file, and prosecute patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support stems from Section 32 of the AIA (Director to work with IP law associations on pro bono programs) and USPTO strategic plan goals to enhance assistance to independent inventors and small businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional program structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional patent pro bono programs (21 across the country) provide matching services and each covers one or more states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional programs are independent of the USPTO and are operated by nonprofits, universities, or bar associations. They follow general USPTO guidelines but set their own policies and procedures, so specifics (e.g., financial thresholds or processes) may vary regionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor eligibility (Patent Pro Bono)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional programs screen applicants for income (less than 300% of the poverty guidelines), requirement of a provisional application on file and/or completion of a certificate training course, and having an actual invention (more than an idea).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional programs may vary guidelines. Inventors must be able to 'describe with particularity how to make, use, or practice your invention.' Training course information is provided (link; available in Spanish).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner requirement (Patent Pro Bono)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only registered patent practitioners can represent financially under-resourced inventors to prepare, file, and prosecute patent applications before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More than 1,600 practitioners have volunteered, but need outpaces supply — emphasizing the registration requirement and demand for volunteers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent practitioner recognition criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO issues certificates to registered patent practitioners who provide 50+ hours of patent pro bono service in a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent practitioner name, firm, and regional program are posted on the USPTO website; certificates are signed by the Commissioner for Patents and the Director for the Office of Enrollment and Discipline. Recognition has been expanded to include consecutive recipients and recipients receive a signature graphic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law firm/corporation recognition criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO recognizes law firms and corporations that support the Patent Pro Bono Program via certificates awarded annually based on cumulative hours per firm/corporation and firm/corporation size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient names are posted on the USPTO website. Law firm hours were expanded to include non-practitioner assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law School Clinic Certification Program requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows students in a participating law school’s clinic to practice before the USPTO under the strict guidance of a Law School Faculty Clinic Supervisor; OED grants participating law students limited recognition to practice before the USPTO in patents/trademarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation gives real-world experience to clinic students while providing IP pro bono services to the community; questions directed to Office of Enrollment and Discipline and FAQs are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB Pro Bono Program scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Assists independent inventors who are financially under-resourced by matching volunteer patent professionals to provide free legal assistance in preparing ex parte appeals to the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program initially handles ex parte appeals only, with possible future expansion to AIA proceedings. Administered by the PTAB Bar Association (clearinghouse model), independent of the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB volunteer practitioner eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Volunteers must be a registered patent practitioner with the USPTO in good standing; attorneys must also be in good standing in any state(s) where they are licensed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional requirements: have experience in the technology and proceeding type, provide malpractice insurance, agree to no fee for services, and provide a representation agreement and termination agreement at completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to volunteer for PTAB Pro Bono
rubrics_metrics.description: Volunteers create an account and log in to the PTAB Bar Association webpage and complete the volunteer application form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application requires personal info, attorney info, law firm info, technology preference, addresses, contact information, languages, electronic signature/date. Provide all required information or application processing may be delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB volunteer processing and matching procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearinghouse enters volunteer information into a database and will contact unmatched volunteers regarding new appeals; volunteer agrees to representation after evaluating the case and completing a conflict check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once matched, the volunteer is removed from the database for the period of ongoing representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB inventor eligibility and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors must be domiciled in the U.S.; gross household income limited to 300% of federal poverty guidelines (limit increases with dependents); micro entity status (75% fee reduction) may apply; must have an appealable rejection in a pending application; and must request assistance within 1 month from the date of the Office action at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventors must demonstrate knowledge of the program and the appeal process by completing a 2-part video training online (Part 1: PTAB Pro Bono Program and application process; Part 2: Overview of ex parte appeals). Federal poverty guidelines are updated yearly; example single-person income cap provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB matching timeline and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB Bar Association will provide practitioners with a brief description of inventor backgrounds and the appeal and aims to make a match within one month after application submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is no match after a month, the PTAB Bar Association will inform the inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of representation for PTAB pro bono cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Volunteer representation is limited to the PTAB proceeding only, through a PTAB decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope explicitly does not include rehearing or appeal to federal courts. Volunteers provide an inventor with a representation agreement and a termination letter once representation is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applying to volunteer with PTAB Pro Bono Program (administrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should apply directly with the PTAB Bar Association (www.ptabbar.org) and visit www.uspto.gov/PTABprobono for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEAP (Legal Experience and Advancement Program) qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Designed to aid development of the next generation of patent practitioners; to qualify, a patent agent or attorney must have three or fewer substantive oral arguments in any federal tribunal, including the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEAP encourages diverse advocates to develop their skills before the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB Pro Bono Program clearinghouse and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: TTAB pro bono provides representation to pro se parties; TTAB sets and publishes standards; clearinghouse organizations match attorneys with clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearinghouse must be nondiscriminatory in assigning attorneys and clients; no clients may be excluded because of conflicts; law firms typically cannot operate as clearinghouses; no fees may be charged for the services; clearinghouse sets financial need standards (no fixed limit in standards); minimal attorney competency standards are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTAB procedural constraints relevant to pro se representation
rubrics_metrics.description: TTAB proceedings differ from trademark examination: the record must be complete before appeal; no evidence can be filed with an appeal brief; an applicant’s position must be limited to the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions and cancellations are more complex; paper-trial processes and resulting rules are challenging and often confuse pro se parties — this underlies the need for pro bono help.
